title: Zephyrine and the Ledger
premise: In the port city of Verrance, on the eve of a war that will empty it, Ada Delacroix is summoned to repair the observatory's master clock and finds a child abandoned at its door with instructions to forget her face. The child's ledger names three families entitled to passage on the last evacuation ship — Ada's estranged mother, the clockmaker who disowned her father, and the child herself. As the city's powerful forge documents to claim berths, Ada must decide whether to restore the clock, and with it the official time by which the ship will sail, or let it stop and buy herself the hours to choose who survives.
about_author: Ivo Yarrow is the pen name of a former horologist's apprentice who spent a decade restoring municipal clocks across coastal Europe before turning to fiction. Their work examines how ordinary people measure loss when history refuses to wait.

chapters.title: The Weight of Small Gears
chapters.summary: Ada, POV first person, arrives in Verrance with a single toolbox and the pride of being summoned above senior apprentices. The observatory's master clock has stopped at an impossible hour. Emotional beat: cautious ambition shadowed by the knowledge that no one summons an invisible person for good reasons.

chapters.title: Instructions in a Stranger's Hand
chapters.summary: At the observatory door Ada finds a girl of six, frozen, clutching a sealed ledger. A note reads: repair the clock, forget the face. Ada's POV; she nearly walks away twice. Emotional beat: fear warring with the recognition of her own childhood abandonment.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Three Names
chapters.summary: Ada breaks the seal: the ledger records entitlements to berths aboard the last ship, the Meridian — one for Mireille Delacroix, her mother; one for Uncle Tomas, her father's brother; one blank line beside the child's name. POV Ada. Emotional beat: vertigo at discovering her family written into someone else's arithmetic.

chapters.title: Orders for Evacuation
chapters.summary: City-wide proclamation: Verrance empties in eleven days. Ada watches neighbors weigh what can be carried. POV shifts to Sergeant Halloran, tasked with verifying passenger lists, who notices the master clock's stoppage threatens the sailing schedule. Emotional beat: civic dread turning transactional.

chapters.title: What Can Be Carried
chapters.summary: Ada repairs the escapement while the child, whom she calls Zephyrine after the wind vane, shadows her. Flashbacks reveal Ada's mother sold her apprenticeship to survive. POV Ada. Emotional beat: tenderness growing where duty was supposed to be.

chapters.title: The Clockmaker Who Disowned a Son
chapters.summary: Uncle Tomas arrives at the observatory, having traced the ledger, and offers Ada legitimacy, tools, a name restored — if she certifies his berth. POV Tomas. Emotional beat: charm curdling into leverage; he sees the child as paperwork.

chapters.title: A Mother in the Queue
chapters.summary: Ada finds Mireille in the ration lines, aged and unrepentant, claiming her berth as owed. Their confrontation reveals Mireille surrendered Ada once already, decades ago, to the same kind of ledger. POV Mireille. Emotional beat: grief weaponized into entitlement.

chapters.title: Halloran's Dilemma
chapters.summary: Halloran discovers forged berth claims flooding the harbor office — the wealthy are buying identities. He needs the master clock running to timestamp authentic manifests. POV Halloran. Emotional beat: a decent man realizing the system he serves runs on corrupted time.

chapters.title: Nine Days
chapters.summary: Ada stalls the repair, lying to both Tomas and Halloran about progress. Zephyrine begins speaking again, revealing fragments: her parents were clerks who kept the true ledger and were silenced for it. POV Ada. Emotional beat: protective fury hardening into resolve.

chapters.title: The Forgers' Guild
chapters.summary: Tomas is revealed as middleman for the document ring selling berths; he needs Ada's certification to launder the worst forgeries. He threatens to report the child as undocumented. POV Tomas. Emotional beat: self-justification — he tells himself everyone is choosing someone over someone.

chapters.title: Zephyrine Remembers
chapters.summary: Through the child's fragmented POV, the night of her abandonment returns: her mother pressed the ledger into her hands because a clerk's daughter could pass where a witness could not. Emotional beat: terror transmuted into the child's quiet understanding that she is evidence.

chapters.title: Seven Days
chapters.summary: Halloran confronts Ada, suspecting the stalled clock is deliberate. She shows him the ledger; he realizes authenticating manifests means certifying the forgeries too. An uneasy alliance forms. POV Halloran. Emotional beat: two keepers of time deciding which time matters.

chapters.title: Mireille's Bargain
chapters.summary: Mireille offers Ada the truth of her father's death in exchange for the berth — he died trying to expose the same ring Tomas serves. POV Mireille. Emotional beat: confession offered as currency; love indistinguishable from blackmail.

chapters.title: The Escapement of Conscience
chapters.summary: Alone at midnight, Ada finishes the repair but holds back one wheel. She rehearses every version of the choice: mother, uncle, child. POV Ada. Emotional beat: the terrible clarity that any choice is also an execution.

chapters.title: Five Days
chapters.summary: Tomas, suspicious, breaks into the observatory and finds the withheld wheel; he takes the ledger. Without it, Zephyrine has no claim at all. POV Ada. Emotional beat: violation and panic — the rules themselves have been stolen.

chapters.title: Halloran's Choice
chapters.summary: Ordered to certify Tomas's manifests, Halloran instead copies the true ledger from memory into the official record, knowing it ends his career and maybe his life. POV Halloran. Emotional beat: a small man performing one incorruptible act.

chapters.title: Three Days
chapters.summary: Ada trades the finished clock — perfect time, guaranteed sailing schedule — to Tomas in exchange for the ledger and his withdrawal. He agrees, believing he has won everything. POV Ada. Emotional beat: cold, deliberate sacrifice of her craft's masterpiece.

chapters.title: The Master Clock Runs
chapters.summary: The clock strikes true for the first time in months; the city moves to its heartbeat toward the ships. Tomas boards triumphant. Mireille waits at the dock, certain of blood's claim. POV alternating Ada/Halloran. Emotional beat: dread beneath apparent order.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: At the gangway, Ada gives the berth to Zephyrine and places the ledger in Halloran's hands as testimony. Mireille begs; Ada finally speaks the truth of her abandonment aloud and lets her go. POV Ada. Emotional beat: severance and release — choosing the future over the past.

chapters.title: What the Clock Struck
chapters.summary: As the Meridian pulls out, soldiers arrive for Tomas, whose forged papers Halloran's record exposed; he is taken off at the pier. Mireille vanishes into the emptied city. POV Halloran. Emotional beat: justice arriving late, partial, and real.

chapters.title: Time Kept
chapters.summary: Ada stays behind with Halloran and the remaining stragglers, winding the master clock through the occupation so that when Verrance is rebuilt, there will be a true hour to return to. Letters arrive from Zephyrine overseas. POV Ada. Emotional beat: mourning braided with purpose.

chapters.title: The Wind Vane Turns
chapters.summary: Years later, Ada trains apprentices of her own, including children nobody claimed. A young woman arrives bearing Zephyrine's grown face and a new ledger — this one recording debts repaid, not owed. POV Ada, closing frame. Emotional beat: inheritance redefined — what we carry forward is not property but witness.
